title: Understanding Your Messi Salary: Hourly to Annual with Casual Loading and Super
description: Learn how to calculate your messi salary from hourly rates to annual pay, including casual loading, superannuation, tax, and fortnightly figures. Use our timesheet tool.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross messi salary is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with casual loading and super paid on top.

faqs.a: A messi salary refers to a pay rate that requires careful calculation due to factors like casual loading, superannuation, and tax. It's not just the hourly rate times hours; you need to account for additional payments and deductions to understand your true annual figure.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual salary?
faqs.a: Casual loading adds 25% to your base hourly rate. For example, if your base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05. Your annual salary is then based on this higher rate, and super is calculated on the ordinary earnings including loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your gross earnings. It is calculated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings (including casual loading if applicable) and is an additional contribution to your super fund, not deducted from your pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## What Is a Messi Salary?

A "messi salary" is a term we use for a pay rate that isn't straightforward—one that involves casual loading, superannuation paid on top, and the usual tax and Medicare deductions. Whether you're a casual employee, a part-timer, or someone comparing a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates into annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay is essential. This guide walks you through the calculations using the latest figures from the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Fair Work Commission, so you can confidently work out your own messi salary.

## The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The foundation of any salary conversion is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard is 38 hours per week. So the formula becomes:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. This is the figure before tax, Medicare, and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The [the timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your own base rate and automatically applies the 38-hour assumption, with an option to add casual loading.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award that may specify higher minimum rates. For instance, the Health Services Award and the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Award have their own classification rates that change from October and December 2026 respectively. Always check the relevant [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman to see the exact rate for your job. Award rates often include allowances and penalty rates that can significantly boost your messi salary.

## Casual Loading: Adding 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. This loading is applied to the minimum award rate or the national minimum wage. For example, the casual National Minimum Wage is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When calculating your annual messi salary as a casual, you should use the loaded rate. Our [the timesheet](/) tool has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading—never enter a rate that already includes the loading; the tool does it for you.

Your annual gross as a casual on the minimum wage would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80. That's a significant difference from the permanent rate. The loading is part of your ordinary earnings, so super is calculated on the loaded amount.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top, Not Deducted

Superannuation guarantee contributions are paid by your employer on top of your gross salary. From 2026–27, the rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual gross is $65,306.80, your employer must contribute an extra $7,836.82 into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay—it's an additional benefit. When comparing a salary offer, remember that the total employment cost includes both your gross pay and the super contribution. For more details, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Fortnightly Pay: Weekly × 2

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay. Using the casual minimum wage example: weekly pay is $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90, so fortnightly is $2,511.80. This is before tax and Medicare. If you're budgeting, knowing your fortnightly figure helps align with typical bill cycles.

## Tax and Medicare: What You Take Home

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, you pay:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a casual on $65,306.80, the tax would be approximately $11,547 plus Medicare $1,306, leaving a take-home of about $52,454 per year, or $1,009 per week. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more precise estimate.

## Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [the timesheet](/) is designed to handle the messi salary calculation. You enter your base hourly rate (the rate before any loading), select whether you're casual to add the 25% loading, and the tool shows your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly gross figures. It also estimates tax and Medicare based on the 2026–27 rates. Remember, the tool assumes a consistent 38-hour week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or salary sacrifice. For award-specific rates, always refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman.

## Why It Matters

Understanding your messi salary helps you negotiate better, compare job offers, and plan your finances. Whether you're a permanent employee on an award rate or a casual with loading, knowing the full picture—including super paid on top—ensures you're not short-changed. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award, and the Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum. Use these official sources alongside our tools to get an accurate estimate.

## Final Thoughts

Calculating your annual salary from an hourly rate is straightforward once you know the assumptions. Always use 38 hours per week unless your award specifies otherwise. Add casual loading if applicable, and remember super is extra. For a quick and reliable estimate, try our [the timesheet](/) tool. And if you're comparing roles, check the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for your industry to see how your messi salary stacks up.
